## Historical audit: S0071, visible chunk 2 of 6

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only the supplied text is audited; neither image is visible here.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Goal and build — line 10, `model_request`, chars [0,194128) | The task requested an editable, single-photo indoor reconstruction. The student’s source modeled separate architecture, window, chaise, pillow, card and foreground chair; parquet, upholstery stripes/flecks and cane strands were geometry with colored finishes. These are modeled interpretations, not independently verified reference contents. |
| Audit input and adoption — line 10, chars [0,194128) | A **user-role source-audit instruction**, not an identified teacher diagnosis, requested checks before execution. The subsequent student program adopted checked constructors, duplicate-key assertions, named-subtree material copying and missing-World initialization; it also rotated the card and printing together and adjusted foot radius. No separate teacher detection or diagnosis is visible. |
| First validation — line 10, chars [0,194128) | The embedded step-1 result reports `ok: true`, a completed render and saved image. A later user instruction requested comparison and a bounded production revision. This is execution evidence, not visual or geometric validation by this audit. |
| Student exploration — lines 11–12, `codex_session` [0,3429), `model_response` [0,14182) | The session received paths for reference and render, with zero tool calls. The student reported a too-small chaise, central crown/feet, sloping molding and insufficient chair cropping. It separately hypothesized camera distance and azimuth as causes. These are student observations and hypotheses, not independently checked pixels. |
| Revision and outcome — lines 13–15, `execute` [0,14871), `execution_result` [0,154168), `select` [0,59) | Step 2 changed camera position and target and rotated the chaise, pillow and card together by −16°; dimensions, finishes and lighting were retained in code. Blender reported `ok: true`, completed rendering, saved an image and blend file; the controller selected step 2. This establishes operational success, not reconstruction correctness. |

**Scene checks and uncertainty.** Multiple semantic objects and materials are present in source, and chaise parts share a parent; the card’s placement and foot heights are explicitly calculated. Those facts do not prove physical contact, correct part connections, occlusion, texture appearance or pose. The student identified framing and wall-line issues and changed camera and pose together, so their separate effects remain unresolved. Lighting is configured and preserved, but its visual adequacy is unknown. The step-2 image and any subsequent visual assessment are not supplied.

**Classification and lessons.** The visible segment shows successful builds and a selected revision, with **overall semantic correctness unknown**; no empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption is evidenced here. Transferable practices include validating primitive parameters and unique keys, isolating shared materials, and distinguishing observations from camera hypotheses. The particular chaise inventory, anchor estimates and rotation are task-specific, not established general rules. The selected render’s resemblance, support contacts, and whether the camera hypothesis was right remain unresolved; unseen chunks cannot resolve them in this audit.
